steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Interest rates set by the Bank of England affect borrowing costs: higher rates = more expensive loans and mortgages, reducing consumer spending and business investment. | Key Fact: Inflation is the general rise in prices over time: high inflation erodes purchasing power and increases business costs, but low stable inflation (2% target) indicates a healthy economy. | Key Fact: Exchange rates affect import/export prices: a stronger pound makes imports cheaper but exports more expensive, hurting UK exporters but helping importers. | Key Fact: The business cycle has four stages: boom (high growth, low unemployment), recession (negative growth, rising unemployment), recovery (growth returns), and slowdown.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Explain how a rise in interest rates from 2% to 5% might affect a business that has a large bank loan. | Analyse how a strengthening of the pound against the euro would affect a UK business that exports to France. | Evaluate whether a recession is always bad for businesses.
